newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil mulls running Europipe II via Denmark.
newsitem.headline: Statoil mulls running Europipe II via Denmark.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) is considering laying the planned Europipe II gas trunkline via western Denmark, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said on Thursday.
The pipeline is proposed to run from Kaarstoe on the west coast of Stavanger to Emden in northern Germany.

Statoil said the diversion would allow gas deliveries to Denmark and Sweden. Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee is already discussing annual sales of up to two billion cubic metres of gas to Dansk Olie og Naturgas from 1999, Statoil said.
"Such a deal would depend on laying Europipe II via Denmark, which would add about 50 kilometres to its overall length and call for additional spending on an additional landfall," Status Weekly said.
"Possible advantages must be balanced against another option: completing the gas line in 1998, a year earlier than first planned, to allow increased sales to continental Europe."

Statoil said that if higher sales to Europe provided better commercial opportunities, the gas line would unlikely be diverted to Denmark. An alternative soultion could be to link Denmark from a standard T joint in Europipe II, Statoil said.
The results of a pilot study into the proposal were expected to be ready next year.
